name: slice_certificate.py
mathematical_scope: Fixed slice h=(1,0,0,x): W reduces to a degree-two polynomial with both GF17 roots checked, and denominator-cleared gate minors are nonzero. If coefficient identities/degrees are exact, nonzero resultant reduction proves no complex common zero on the full regular slice.
input_and_guard_coverage: Assumes W has degree <=2 in x and z is a primitive eighth root; first is a comment rather than an executable generic check. Nonzero Delta/T asserted at two roots; h0=0/Delta=0/T=0 general branches stay open.
costs: Fixed small-field enumeration of 17 x values and two fixed-size determinants; no large-N complexity statement.
test_evidence: Exact field expected polynomial [10,14,16], roots [2,12], and minors [3,2] cross-checked by suite when run. Writes certificate as side effect.
acceptance_boundary: The resultant argument is sound in an integral cyclotomic ring with retained degree/integral coefficient hypotheses. No direct reduction of arbitrary complex roots is assumed. Narrow regular slice only.
findings: L25–29 interpolation of three values alone would not certify degree<=2; saved W coefficients inspected here do contain x-degree at most two. L65 manually labels W=0 from the root condition rather than separately reevaluating it.
